importance_evaluation.scientific_significance: Pioneered quantitative experimental physics, formulated the classical law of falling bodies, established classical principle of relativity, and advanced observational astronomy using the telescope.
importance_evaluation.historical_significance: Central figure of the Scientific Revolution who challenged Aristotelian physics and promoted the heliocentric Copernican model, leading to fundamental transformations in scientific methodology and institutional natural philosophy.

timeline_a_biological.event: Born in Pisa, Duchy of Florence, to Vincenzo Galilei and Giulia Ammannati.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Parish registration records in Pisa confirm February 15, 1564.

timeline_a_biological.event: Enrolled at the University of Pisa to study medicine.
Appointed Chair of Mathematics at the University of Pisa.
Appointed Professor of Mathematics at the University of Padua.
Appointed Chief Mathematician and Philosopher to the Grand Duke of Tuscany in Florence.
Tried by the Roman Inquisition, forced to recant heliocentrism, and placed under permanent house arrest.

timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Historical records of death on January 8, 1642.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Wrote 'La Bilancetta' ('The Little Balance'), describing an accurate hydrostatic balance.
Formulated the law that distance fallen under uniform gravity is proportional to the square of time ($s \propto t^2$).
timeline_b_scientific.evidence_note: Letter to Paolo Sarpi in October 1604.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Published 'Sidereus Nuncius' detailing observations of lunar topography, Galilean moons of Jupiter, and phases of Venus.
timeline_b_scientific.evidence_note: Published text printing in Venice, March 1610.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Published 'Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems' comparing Copernican and Ptolemaic models.
Published 'Two New Sciences' in Leiden, summarizing kinematics, uniform acceleration, projectile motion, and strength of materials.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Law of Falling Bodies and Uniform Acceleration
physics_analysis.historical_claim: Heavy and light objects fall with the same constant acceleration in a vacuum, and distance traversed grows proportionally to the square of elapsed time.
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Aristotelian physics posited that fall velocity is proportional to weight ($v \propto w$) and inversely proportional to medium density.
physics_analysis.historical_hypothesis: In the absence of medium resistance, all bodies experience uniform acceleration regardless of weight.
physics_analysis.historical_model_or_framework: Kinematic description utilizing geometric proportional reasoning and the odd-number rule ($1, 3, 5, 7, \dots$).
physics_analysis.modern_interpretation: Under constant gravitational field $g$ without drag, $d(t) = \frac{1}{2}g t^2$ and $v(t) = g t$.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Inclined plane experiments with bronze balls rolling along smooth grooved wooden tracks to dilute gravity and permit accurate time measurement via water clocks.

equations.validity_domain: Constant vertical gravitational field without air resistance.
equations.assumptions: Air drag is negligible; uniform gravitational field strength.

equations.validity_domain: Classical mechanics in uniform gravitational field without aerodynamic drag.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Overthrew Aristotelian dynamics, established kinematics as a quantitative science, and laid foundation for Newtonian mechanics.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Neglects drag effects; invalid at relativistic speeds or varying gravitational fields.
physics_analysis.verification_note: Detailed notes and calculations survive in Galileo's Working Papers (Ms. Gal. 72).

physics_analysis.historical_claim: The motion of a projectile is a combination of uniform horizontal inertial motion and uniformly accelerated vertical motion, generating a parabolic path.
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Medieval and Aristotelian dynamics posited distinct phases of motion (impetus phase, transition curve, and vertical straight drop).
physics_analysis.historical_hypothesis: Horizontal and vertical motion components operate independently of one another.
physics_analysis.historical_model_or_framework: Geometric decomposition of compound orthogonal motions.
physics_analysis.modern_interpretation: Vector decomposition: $x(t) = v_{0x} t$, $y(t) = v_{0y} t - \frac{1}{2}g t^2$, describing a parabola $y(x) = \frac{v_{0y}}{v_{0x}}x - \frac{g}{2 v_{0x}^2} x^2$.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Horizontal deflection of spheres rolling off elevated surfaces and deflected inclined planes.

variables_definition.a: constant coefficient dependent on initial velocity and gravity

equations.validity_domain: Flat-Earth approximation under uniform gravity without drag.
equations.assumptions: No atmospheric drag, independence of horizontal and vertical components.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: First accurate mathematical description of ballistic motion; precursor to classical vector superposition.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Inaccurate over long distances where atmospheric drag is substantial or earth curvature matters.
physics_analysis.verification_note: Formally demonstrated in Day Four of 'Two New Sciences' (1638).

physics_analysis.historical_claim: The mechanical laws of physics are identical in all non-accelerating (inertial) frames of reference.
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Objection to Copernican system: if Earth moved, observers on Earth would experience constant hurricane-force winds and discarded objects would fall far behind.
physics_analysis.historical_hypothesis: Experiments performed inside a smoothly moving enclosed system (e.g., inside a ship) yield identical results regardless of constant system speed.
physics_analysis.historical_model_or_framework: Thought experiment involving a ship at rest versus a ship moving smoothly across water.
physics_analysis.modern_interpretation: Galilean transformations: $x' = x - vt, y' = y, z' = z, t' = t$. Physical laws are invariant under Galilean boosts.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Thought experiment outlined in 'Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems' (1632) involving butterflies, fish, falling drops of water inside a ship cabin.

equations.assumptions: Absolute universal time; rigid inertial coordinate frames.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Removed main mechanical objections to Earth's orbital and rotational motion; foundation for Newton's First Law.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Fails at near-light-speed scales (requires Lorentz transformations) and in non-inertial frames.
physics_analysis.verification_note: Explicitly detailed in the Second Day of the 'Dialogue' (1632).

major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: Galileo did not invent the telescope; he improved existing Dutch spyglass designs in 1609 and applied them systematically to astronomical observation.

major_claims_audit.claim: Galileo dropped weights from the Leaning Tower of Pisa to prove falling speed is independent of mass.
major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: The Leaning Tower experiment was reported by his biographer Vincenzo Viviani, but historical consensus views it as either a public demonstration or a rhetorical depiction rather than his primary method of discovery, which relied on inclined plane experiments.

major_claims_audit.claim: Galileo was the first to invent the scientific method.
major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: Galileo was a major pioneer in integrating mathematical modeling with controlled experimentation, but the development of scientific methodology was a cumulative process with many precursors.

major_claims_audit.claim: Galileo discovered the moons of Jupiter.
major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: Galileo was the first to discover and record observations of the four largest moons of Jupiter (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) in January 1610.

verified_sources.title: Galileo Galilei: Sidereus Nuncius
verified_sources.supported_claim: First telescopic observations of the Moon, Galilean satellites of Jupiter, and stars.

verified_sources.title: Discourses and Mathematical Demonstrations Relating to Two New Sciences
verified_sources.supported_claim: Kinematics of falling bodies, parabolic trajectories, strength of materials.

verified_sources.title: Galileo at Work: His Scientific Biography
verified_sources.supported_claim: Historical reconstruction of inclined plane experiments and mathematical developments.

major_uncertainties: Exact details and historical reality of the Leaning Tower of Pisa public demonstration.
Precise chronology of early pendulum studies at Pisa versus later formalization.
high_risk_claims: Attributing the invention of the telescope to Galileo.
Describing Galileo as the sole creator of the scientific method.
